clue.text: Put one's foot down before end of movie in flight

parts.note: to put one's foot down heavily is to stamp, here in the past tense

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so take the last letter of movie

explanation.surface: Someone stamps their foot just before a film finishes, perhaps on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is not air travel but headlong running away, as of panicked cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of animals or people, a mass flight.

clue.text: Dry garden — three quarters of it you need to pull out

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: keeping three of the four letters means dropping one, the last

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that most of a parched plot needs weeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three quarters of' drops the last of EDEN's four letters, leaving EDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to withdraw formally from a union or federation.

clue.text: Appropriate stone finally used in building extension

parts.note: to annex is to seize or take over territory

indicators.note: the final letter of the word stone is taken

explanation.surface: A builder uses a suitable stone to finish an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building or wing added onto a main one.

clue.text: Bogus soak hung about

indicators.note: hung is placed about, that is surrounding, the word for soak

parts.note: pended is an old word for hung or dangled
to ret is to soak flax or hemp in water

explanation.surface: A drunk lingers around, looking like a fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' suggests a drunk; RET is the verb for soaking flax to soften it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretended can mean feigned or sham, so pretended feelings are false ones.

clue.text: Rash, a very medical complication

indicators.note: a complication tangles things, so the letters of the fodder are mixed up

explanation.surface: A patient's skin rash turns out to be a serious medical complication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complication' rearranges A VERY MEDICAL. 'Rash' looks like a skin condition but means reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-may-care means recklessly unconcerned about consequences, which is rash behaviour.

clue.text: In a ship, top of funnel looks black

indicators.note: the clue places the funnel top inside the abbreviation for a ship, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a cowl is the hood fitted over the top of a chimney or ship's funnel

explanation.surface: A description of a smoky steamer whose funnel is darkening the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of funnel' looks like an instruction to take F; it is a cowl, the hood on a funnel.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown angrily, so scowls are black looks.

clue.text: Shy, uplifting creature

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
read as up lifting: the word up raised, which in a down clue reads upwards

explanation.surface: A timid but cheering animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' is split into UP and 'lifting': UP turned upwards in a down answer gives PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent, a water-loving animal.

clue.text: Methodist put up (yes!) a school in the North West

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top
the reply and the school are set inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: NW is the abbreviation for north-west
aye is an old or Scottish word for yes
the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A Methodist enthusiastically agrees to found a school in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns the whole assembly upside down, so it reads from the bottom of the light; 'yes!' is the Scots or nautical affirmative, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesleyan Methodism follows John Wesley, founder of the Methodist movement.

clue.text: Dogs are loose some days

indicators.note: loose letters are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some days the dogs get off the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges SOME DAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoyeds are a Siberian breed of fluffy white sled dog.

clue.text: Trick shot used in tennis in a jam

parts.note: to trick or swindle someone is to con them
the serve is the opening stroke in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player with a crafty stroke gets out of a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a jam' suggests trouble, but jam is the definition, the fruit preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A conserve is a preserve of fruit boiled with sugar, much like jam.

clue.text: Servant takes money for a mineral

parts.note: a gyp is a college servant at Cambridge or Durham
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A domestic servant is paid for some fizzy drink or rock.
explanation.walkthrough: GYP is Cambridge slang for a college servant, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft mineral, calcium sulphate, used for plaster.

clue.text: Incident with man embraced by enchanting woman

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the enchantress's name

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress in Homer's Odyssey
cum is Latin for with
Stan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tale of a man caught up in a sorceress's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: CUM, the Latin for with, as in 'kitchen-cum-diner', is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A circumstance is a fact or event, a particular occurrence or happening.

clue.text: Some states go to pot

explanation.surface: A comment on how parts of a country are going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie names the American southern states, and a dixie is also a large army cooking pot.

clue.text: Flowers made into a garland without doubt, without haste

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
surely means certainly, without doubt

explanation.surface: Someone takes their time stringing a flower garland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' looks like rivers in crossword style, but here it is literal: a lei is woven flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried, done at a relaxed pace.

clue.text: Loan given to BR employee for a van

parts.note: an advance is money lent ahead of time
a guard works on trains of BR, British Rail

explanation.surface: A railway worker borrows money to buy a delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway. 'van' is not a vehicle but the front of an army, short for vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The van, short for vanguard, is the leading body of an advancing force.

clue.text: "The King and I" — big finale is magnificent

annotationWithheld.why: "The King and I" — big finale is magnificent (9): GR + AND + I gives GRANDI, but no reading of 'big finale is' found for OSE (big = OS, outsize, leaves E without a clear source)
annotationWithheld.clue: "The King and I" — big finale is magnificent

clue.text: Take tea with showgirl and new president

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Irma la Douce is the title character of a stage musical

explanation.surface: A newly elected head of state has tea with a chorus girl.
explanation.walkthrough: IRMA is Irma la Douce, the Parisian girl of the musical and film.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairman presides over a meeting or company, acting as its president.

clue.text: Feeling beholden -for some coal?

explanation.surface: Someone thankful when the fire is stoked.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words: a fireplace filled with coal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means thankful, under obligation; split, it is a fireplace grate brimming with fuel.

clue.text: Bedroom chats can make you unfit

indicators.note: the letters of these clue words can be made into something else, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A warning that late-night pillow talk will wear you out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges BEDROOM CHATS. The answer is the French phrase for a soldier put out of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Hors de combat is French for out of the fight, disabled and unable to take part.

clue.text: Bend a fastening

explanation.surface: A clasp is twisted out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle is to bend or crumple under strain, and a buckle is a clasp for a belt or strap.

clue.text: Secluded offices erected

indicators.note: something erected stands upright, so in a down clue it reads upwards

parts.note: terce is one of the daily church offices, the service of the third hour

explanation.surface: A hidden office block has been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offices' looks like workplaces but means church services; TERCES read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret place is one hidden away, private and secluded.

clue.text: Re edit, reprint, and, for the French, reword

indicators.note: to re-edit text is to rework it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: A publisher's instruction list: edit, reprint and translate into French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re edit' (printed Re-edit) rearranges REPRINT plus ET to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret can mean to render in other words or translate, as rewording does.

clue.text: Creatures with one horn, possibly

parts.note: suggests the unicorn, but describes a real animal, some of which have a single horn

explanation.definitionFit: The Indian rhinoceros has a single horn, so rhinos are beasts that may bear just one.

clue.text: A devil or two

explanation.surface: A remark about a little mischief, or a couple of demons.
explanation.definitionFit: The deuce is a mild name for the devil, and a deuce is a playing card or die face showing two.

clue.text: Rabbit — one name is a bun

parts.note: a rabbit is a poor player, a duffer; a muff is likewise a clumsy bungler
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pet rabbit's name turns out to be that of a baked treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like an animal, but in sporting slang a rabbit is an incompetent player, as is a muff.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a small soft bread roll or cake, a kind of bun.

clue.text: Seem to interrupt expert witness

indicators.note: one word breaking into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a oner is an expert or outstanding person
to look a certain way is to seem so

explanation.surface: An expert witness is told to appear to interrupt proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: ONER, an old slang word for an expert, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a bystander who sees an event, a witness to it.

clue.text: The admiral's in the hold

explanation.surface: A naval commander is down below in the ship's cargo hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Nelson is Britain's most famous admiral, and a nelson is a wrestling grip.

clue.text: Forceful and virile people introduced to surgeon

indicators.note: one piece brought into another is placed inside it

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
he-men are strongly masculine men

explanation.surface: Some macho types meet a doctor, perhaps for a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgeon' points to a doctor, but the letters come from a veterinary surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means intense and passionate, as a forceful protest is.
